findings.title: Task 2.2's "both groups non-empty" real-file assertion cannot pass against the interim fixture
findings.description: Task 2.2 requires a real-file test "asserting both groups are non-empty and their counts sum to the file's checkbox count," using `384-tasks.post-findings-to-the-pr.md` "until then" (i.e. until 385's own file has checked items). I verified by grep that 384's file has **no `- [ ]` lines at all** — every checkbox is `- [x]` (status: complete) — so its `unchecked` group is empty and the "both groups are non-empty" assertion fails against the named interim fixture. The other candidate, 385's own file at authoring time, is entirely unchecked (status: not_started), so its `checked` group is empty and it fails the same assertion. The technical success criterion only guarantees "a test fixture using this slice's own task file **once it exists**" — mid-implementation — and never guarantees both groups in the interim. As specified, the load-bearing real-file test is un-passable when Task 2.2 lands, contradicting CLAUDE.md's "the test fixture must include the actual format that parser will consume in production." Fix: either seed a real file containing mixed states, or restate the success assertion to "both groups' counts sum to the file's checkbox total" (dropping the non-empty requirement), or defer the real-file assertion to Task 16 after items are checked off.

findings.title: Task 6 consumes a `local_sha` that no task or helper produces
findings.description: `check_head_pushed(..., local_sha: str, ...)` compares the host sha against a *local* head sha for the "behind" refusal (D2). Task 3 (the git-helpers task) adds `current_branch` and `commits_in_range` only — neither returns the local HEAD sha. Task 13.1's data-flow bullet ("preconditions … local head sha == remote sha") names the comparison but does not assign its read. No task writes a `git rev-parse HEAD` helper, so a junior implementer must either invent a read or silently reuse `resolve_reviewed_sha` (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py:132`), which returns `str | None` and is not mentioned anywhere in the slice or tasks. This leaves the task not independently completable and forces an implicit dependency on a `None`-returning helper into a strict-typed signature (`local_sha: str`). Fix: add a `local_head_sha` (or state reuse of `resolve_reviewed_sha`, handling its `None`) as an explicit step in Task 3 and thread it through Task 13.1.

findings.title: Identity precondition (`identify_operator` no-login refusal) has tests but no implementation step
findings.description: The functional criterion "With the adapter unable to identify the operator, the command exits non-zero, names the reason, and makes no write" and the design's precondition block (`identify_operator(host)` → no login → refuse, exit 1) require an identity check. It is covered by tests (Task 13.2 "identity refusal exits 1 with no write"; Task 14.1 parametrizes the `identify_operator` site), but no implementation step tells the worker where the call and its refusal are written. Task 6 is scoped only to the pushed-branch checks; Task 13.1 mentions identity solely inside the ordering bullet "preconditions (identity, then pushed)" without a step, success clause, or exit-1 behavior. The implementation requirement is thus met only by inference from the tests, so an implementer may miss the no-login `OperatorUnidentifiedError` path until Task 13.2 fails. Fix: add an explicit step (in Task 6 or 13.1) that calls `identify_operator`, renders a refusal via `render_code_host_error`, and exits before the base/model work.

findings.title: `git rev-list` membership source for the review scan (Task 8) is unstated
findings.description: Task 8.1 says "Keep those whose sha is in `git rev-list <base>..<head>`," but no task adds a `rev-list` helper. The in-range sha set is already derivable from `commits_in_range`'s return (Task 3, which lists exactly the `base..head` commits), so membership is `sha in {c.sha for c in commits}`. The instruction is satisfiable without a new helper, but naming the source would prevent a redundant second git call. Non-blocking.

findings.title: Functional criterion's "the same command" conflicts with D2's two different commands
findings.description: The functional criterion says a behind-branch "fails the same way with the same command," but D2 explicitly prescribes `git push -u <remote> <head>` for *missing* and `git push <remote> <head>` for *behind*, and Task 6.2 asserts "the two refusals name different commands." The tasks faithfully implement the authoritative design; the slice's summary prose is the sloppy line. Flagging so a future reviewer does not re-open this as a task gap — the task is correct, the criterion wording is imprecise.

findings.title: `tests/pr/` package is created without an `__init__.py`
findings.description: Seven test files land under `tests/pr/` but no task creates `tests/pr/__init__.py`. Every substantive test subpackage in the repo carries one (`tests/codehost`, `tests/review`, `tests/cli/commands`, …), so this deviates from convention. Risk is low because `pyproject.toml` sets no `import-mode` and I confirmed no basename collisions with existing `test_branch/tasks/base/body/inputs/assembly/preconditions.py` (none exist), and `tests/load`/`tests/scripts` already ship without `__init__.py`. Non-blocking; add the marker file in Task 1.2 for consistency.
